newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada auto workers halt talks with Chrysler.
newsitem.headline: Canada auto workers halt talks with Chrysler.

text.p: Canadian Auto Workers President Buzz Hargrove said on Monday the union was halting talks with Chrysler Corp's Canadian unit until it could resolve the key issue of outsourcing.
"We're not moving any further until we resolve this issue," Hargrove told reporters.

He said it will be difficult to conclude an agreement on all issues by the Tuesday strike deadline. "The clock has become our enemy and it is very difficult for us to conclude an agreement on all issues ahead of 11:59 (EDT) on Tuesday," Hargrove said.

Chrysler officials said they remained optimistic that they could avert a strike. "We're still relatively optimistic things can be resolved prior to the strike deadline, a little over 24 hours away," said Othmar Stein, a spokesman for Chyrsler Canada Ltd.
Stein said there was room for the company to move on the outsourcing issue but that it was tied to other issues which the CAW has stalled.
"There is always room to move on any of these issues but again it depends on how they tie into other issues of equal importance to us," he said.
However, Stein would not specify what those issues were.

Hargrove left after a short press conference for a caucus with the heads of the various committees of the union and said he would talk to Chrysler's lead negotiator Ken Francese about any possible further movement on outsourcing.
